newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks pass 8,000 pts, close at 6-yr high.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks pass 8,000 pts, close at 6-yr high.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Wednesday, slicing through the 8,000-point resistance level to set a six-year high as investors showed confidence in market-boosting comments by government officials, brokers said.
The index ended up 62.89 points, or 0.79 percent, at 8,019.46, after it had reached an intra-day high of 8,049.94.
Wednesday's close surpassed the 7,983.71 finish on Saturday and marked the index's highest level since it reached 8,059.14 on May 16, 1990.
Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Lu Tung-ying said on late Tuesday that the market's heavy turnover was acceptable as long as the bourse remained in order.

"Positive statements by government officials were the major reason for the gains," said George Hou, fund manager at Jardine Fleming. "Investor confidence was renewed after being dampened by the central bank's call for caution."
The transport sector, boosted by prospects of direct shipping between Taiwan and China, surged 3.07 percent -- with First Steamship rising T$1.60 to close at T$25.50.
Chemical issues rose 2.08 percent, with China Chemical up T$2.10 to T$34.80.
Automobiles were the only losing sector, falling 0.42 percent due to profit-taking by investors, brokers said.
Analysts said they expected the market to rise further in the near term.
For Thursday, a 7,900-8,200 trading range was seen.
